title: Core ideas in chemistry
description: How atoms, bonds and reactions work, and how to read the periodic table.

ideas.title: Atoms and elements
ideas.summary: An atom is a nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons around it, and the proton count sets the element.

items.q: What does the atomic number of an element count?
items.a: The number of protons in the nucleus of each of its atoms

items.q: In chemistry, what are isotopes?
items.a: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons

items.q: In chemistry, what is an ion?
items.a: An atom or molecule with a net electric charge, from gaining or losing electrons

items.q: Which element has atomic number 6?

ideas.title: The periodic table
ideas.summary: Set out in order of atomic number, the elements fall into columns whose members behave alike.

items.q: Which Russian chemist published his periodic table of the elements in 1869?
What are the vertical columns of the periodic table called?
What name is given to group 18 of the periodic table, the unreactive gases such as helium, neon and argon?
Why do elements in the same group of the periodic table tend to react in similar ways?
items.a: They have similar valence-electron configurations, which govern much of their chemical behavior

ideas.title: Chemical bonds
ideas.summary: Atoms join by sharing or handing over electrons, and the kind of bond shapes how the substance behaves.

items.q: What kind of chemical bond forms when two atoms share a pair of electrons?
What kind of chemical bond forms when one atom hands electrons to another, as in table salt?
What is the chemical formula of table salt?
Which attraction between water molecules gives water its unusually high boiling point?

ideas.title: The mole and reactions
ideas.summary: A reaction rearranges atoms without making or destroying any, and the mole is how chemists count them.

items.q: What is Avogadro's number, the number of particles in one mole?
What does the law of conservation of mass say about a chemical reaction?
items.a: The total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants

items.q: What is the balanced equation for hydrogen gas burning in oxygen to make water?
What is the approximate molar mass of water, H2O?

ideas.title: Energy, rate and equilibrium
ideas.summary: A reaction gives out or takes in energy, runs at some rate, and may settle into a balance of both directions.

items.q: What is a chemical reaction called that releases heat to its surroundings?
What does a catalyst do to a chemical reaction?
items.a: It speeds the reaction up by lowering the activation energy, without being used up

items.q: In chemistry, what is dynamic equilibrium?
items.a: Forward and reverse reactions run at equal rates, so the concentrations stay constant

items.q: What does Le Chatelier's principle say about a chemical system at equilibrium?
items.a: If a change is imposed on it, the system shifts in the direction that counteracts the change

ideas.title: Acids and bases
ideas.summary: Acids give up hydrogen ions and bases accept them, and pH measures the balance on a logarithmic scale.

items.q: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
In dilute aqueous solutions at 25 °C, which pH values mark a solution as acidic?
In a dilute aqueous solution, approximately how does hydrogen ion concentration change when pH drops by one unit?
In the Bronsted-Lowry definition, what is an acid?
items.a: A proton donor: a substance that gives up a hydrogen ion
